qs.q: When analyzing the Victory School Club Membership System developed for the KCSE 2025 Computer Studies Project, what core operational objective must the database fulfill?
o: Scheduling facility maintenance routines across all campus athletic training venues.
Generating automated daily attendance reports for core academic classroom lessons.
Processing administrative payroll distributions for external sports coaching staff members.
Managing cafeteria meal planning inventories and student account balances securely.
Automating the tracking and management of student participation in co-curricular activities.
qs.e: The database platform is explicitly designed to streamline and manage student participation in school co-curricular activities.

qs.q: While designing the Victory School Club Membership System, the developer emphasizes innovative database management. Which feature is essential for managing student club memberships effectively?
o: Digital signature verification for official student government election ballots.
Encrypted messaging protocols for direct faculty-to-parent disciplinary notices.
Real-time GPS tracking of students traveling to external sports competitions.
Automated financial auditing tools for school budget allocation oversight.
Relational data tables linking student profiles directly to specific club activities.

qs.q: The Victory School Club Membership System project requires database normalization. What is the primary functional benefit of applying normalization principles to student club records?
o: Accelerating network packet transmission speeds across school Wi-Fi routers.
Encrypting student personal health information against unauthorized cyber intrusions.
Compressing database file sizes to fit within minimal local storage limits.
Eliminating data redundancy and preventing update anomalies across related tables.
Converting relational database queries into object-oriented programming syntax.
qs.e: Database normalization ensures data integrity by removing redundant entries and preventing anomalies during updates.

qs.q: In developing the Victory School Club Membership System, a student programmer designs user authentication levels. Why is role-based access control crucial for this database application?
o: It prevents the database from accepting entries from mobile smartphone devices.
It ensures that all students possess equal editing privileges across records.
It automatically logs out users after five minutes of keyboard inactivity.
It encrypts student club attendance passwords using outdated hash algorithms.
It restricts sensitive administrative functions, such as member deletion, to staff.
qs.e: Role-based access control secures the database by ensuring only authorized users can perform administrative tasks.

qs.q: When testing the Victory School Club Membership System, a developer simulates multiple concurrent user logins. What database property must be maintained to prevent data corruption during simultaneous updates?
o: Database concurrency control and transaction isolation integrity.
Client-side CSS rendering compatibility across legacy web browsers.
High-resolution graphical user interface scaling for mobile displays.
Automated translation of SQL queries into spoken audio output.
Permanent caching of all historical student club attendance records.
qs.e: Concurrency control and transaction isolation are vital database properties ensuring simultaneous edits do not corrupt data.

qs.q: In the Victory School Club Membership System project, data input forms must validate user entries. What is the primary clinical or administrative risk of omitting input validation in this database?
o: Increased electricity consumption by the school server cooling fans.
Slower monitor refresh rates during student ID card barcode scanning.
Injection attacks or malformed data corrupting the integrity of student records.
Accidental permanent deletion of the computer science teacher's grading files.
Automatic conversion of all student names into numerical identification codes.
qs.e: Omitting input validation exposes databases to malformed entries and security vulnerabilities like injection attacks.
